featured_reviews.review_text:
Review Date : 16th August, 2024

I am a 10th passout (87%) from this school. I’ve been studying here from Jr. KG up to class 10. The school provided a great learning experience before the pandemic. However, post-pandemic, there have been some changes that affected my experience.
While the earlier years had excellent teachers and a supportive environment, frequent changes in teachers in later years impacted the continuity of learning.The classrooms could benefit from some updates, and free access to the library would enhance the learning experience.
Additionally, the sports options are somewhat limited, and the costs for camps and picnics might be a bit high for some families.
(The SSC board curriculum has areas that could be improved, and considering a shift to CBSE (it used to be) might address some of these concerns)

Overall, the school continues to offer a good education, there are opportunities for improving the overall experience for students.

featured_reviews.name: Satish Chaurasiya
featured_reviews.review_text:
👩🏻‍🎓Admission & Eligibility:
Best suited for students with a decent percentage and rank in MHT-CET or JEE.
75% attendance is mandatory.
Students involved in technical activities like projects, hackathons, etc., can get grace attendance.

👩🏻‍💻Technical & Co-curricular Activities:
Plenty of extra technical activities available,
Students can join TEJAS, RAW, and more to showcase their talent at national-level competitions.
Every department has its own students’ association that manages events and activities at the department level.
Numerous extra-curricular activities are provided, though students need to actively search and join them.

🫂Scholarships & Financial Support:
Various scholarships are available for students from different categories.
The college helps students with the education loan process.

🏋🏻‍♀️Sports Facilities:
Sports rooms are open after 3 PM.
Students can also play during free lectures or by bunking (although not encouraged).
Sports include Kabaddi, Badminton, Carrom, Chess, and occasionally Cricket & Football etc. Once a year sports competitions are also organised by the sports committee.

🏭Industrial Exposure:
Each department conducts Industrial Visits as part of the academic curriculum.
Project competitions are organized once a year with minimal entry charges, and participants get meals from the college itself on that day.
Internships are available, but students must personally reach out to industries as their interest.

🤑Placements & Career Support:
Placements starts from 7th to 8th semester until all students are placed.
The Training & Placement Officer (TPO) supports all deserving candidates.
Placement packages depend on skills and experience, not comparable to IITs, but decent opportunities exist.
To be placement-ready:
Do at least two internships.
Focus on aptitude and technical preparation from the third year onward.
For Higher study any assistance, also avilable through college itself.

🏛️Infrastructure & Facilities:
Infrastructure is average but satisfactory.
Air-conditioning is available only for the library, labs, and first-year students, with plans to expand to all batches.
Library is large with a wide range of books.
Canteen food is good quality but expensive.
There is a xerox centre on campus which is cheaper than outside stationery.

🚉Accessibility & Location:
The college is at a walkable distance from Dahisar station.
Students can also reach via bus from Borivali station.
Autorickshaw is available from both station.
Concession on First & Second class tickets till age 25.

🏕️Campus Life & Enjoyment
SFIT offers a balanced environment with fun and academics, lush greenery campus. Accessible lift for all students.
Games, picnics, tours, seminars, DJ nights, annual functions, traditional day and more things.
Of course, also assignments, exams, and academic challenges.

📜Final Recommendation:
SFIT is a good choice for ambitious students who didn’t make it to IITs or NITs.
With hard work, discipline, and cooperation with faculty, you can achieve your goals here.

Check the official website for more details and updates.

I'm from the BE Electrical Department 24-25 batch. I have good experience in SFIT, whatever I have written, it's my personal view based on my experience in engineering college.

featured_reviews.review_text:
College Review – Universal College of Engineering

Pros:
Honestly, none worth mentioning—except a few good teachers who are supportive and understanding.

Cons:

Horrendous Access Road:
Reaching the college feels like going through a battlefield. If you're on a bike, prepare for headaches—literally. The road is full of potholes, and the dust is unbearable. You’ll need to wrap yourself up like a mummy just to survive the ride.

Hellish Summers & Exam Setup:
During summer, the college feels like a concentration camp. The worst part? During exams, they often make you sit on the stairs with no fan, no ventilation—just heat and misery.

Printer? More Like a Celebrity:
There’s only one printer in the entire college. Need a printout? Be ready to queue up like it’s a Bhandara outside a temple. You might get your turn, you might not.

Overcrowded Chaos:
IT, CS and AIML students all share the same recess. The result? Overcrowded corridors, packed staircases, and a canteen that serves  disappointing food which no one can enjoy in peace.

Zero Social Life:
Social life here is non-existent. There’s no real place to hang out nearby. It feels like you’re stuck in the set of Maze Runner—surrounded by hills and isolation.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Thakur college complex is very unique place for students of different streems. Thakur College of Science and Commerce, Kandivali
Thakur College of Science and Commerce is one of the well-known colleges in the western suburbs of Mumbai and is popular among students for commerce, management, and science courses. The college has a good reputation for maintaining discipline and providing a balanced environment for both academics and extracurricular activities.
The infrastructure of the college is quite impressive. Classrooms are spacious and well maintained, and many of them are equipped with modern teaching facilities such as projectors and air-conditioning. The library is well stocked with academic books and digital resources, which helps students in their studies and research. The campus also has a clean canteen, laboratories for science and IT students, and an auditorium where seminars, workshops, and cultural programs are organized.
Faculty members are generally experienced and supportive. Most teachers try to explain concepts clearly and encourage students to participate in projects, presentations, and academic discussions. The college also organizes guest lectures and industry-related events that help students gain practical knowledge.
Campus life is active and vibrant. Various cultural festivals, competitions, and sports events are organized throughout the year, giving students opportunities to showcase their talents and build confidence. The diverse student community also makes the college environment lively and engaging.
Placement opportunities are decent, especially for commerce, management, and IT courses. Several companies visit the campus for recruitment, and students also get internship opportunities during their studies.
Overall, Thakur College is a good choice for students looking for quality education in Mumbai with a mix of academics, activities, and career opportunities.

featured_reviews.name: Aayushi
featured_reviews.review_text:
My experience at Thakur College of Science and Commerce has been very mixed, but honestly more negative than positive. While a few teachers are genuinely supportive and knowledgeable, a large number of faculty members lack proper teaching approach and student understanding.
Many teachers tend to shout at students instead of guiding them calmly. Rather than helping when students ask questions or share academic problems, some respond with scolding or dismissive behaviour. This creates an environment where students feel stressed and sometimes even scared to speak up.
In practical sessions especially, students are often criticised harshly even when they are still learning or have not been properly trained beforehand. Instead of mentoring and explaining mistakes, the focus sometimes feels more on discipline than education. There is also a lack of proper event management and coordination during college activities, which affects the overall student experience.
College life should be about learning, growth, and support. Teachers play a huge role in shaping students’ confidence, so respectful communication and guidance are very important. I genuinely hope the college focuses more on improving teaching methods, student support systems, and overall communication between faculty and students.
That said, there are a few good teachers who truly care and make a positive difference, and they deserve appreciation.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to Thakur College for the SBI Clerk exam. The center is good overall, but one thing I didn’t like was the space on the tables — it wasn’t sufficient, and it was difficult to properly place the question paper. Apart from that, the location is convenient: from Kandivali East station, you can take a shared auto for ₹20, which drops you right near the college within 2 minutes. The college itself is nice and clean, and the staff’s behavior was good.

However, the admit card mentioned entry from Gate No. 5, but after asking around, I was told to go further ahead where the entry was from the ground area. Because of this, we had to stand for quite some time under the sun. Other than that, everything was fine.
